content.title: About
content.content: Pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan) is a legume grown in tropical and subtropical regions, native to India or Africa. It is eaten as dried split peas (toor or arhar dal), as whole dried peas, and as fresh green peas in the pod. Pigeon peas have a nutty, earthy flavor and are a staple in Indian, Caribbean, and African cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pigeon peas are among the most important legume crops in India, where they are made into toor dal.
In the Caribbean and Latin America, green pigeon peas are called gandules and are used in rice dishes such as arroz con gandules.
The plant tolerates drought and poor soils and helps enrich the soil with nitrogen.
Pigeon peas can be eaten fresh and green or dried.
They have been cultivated for thousands of years.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Pigeon peas provide protein, making them a staple in many plant-based diets.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Pigeon peas are high in fiber, which supports digestion and fullness.

items.title: Provides folate and iron
items.content: These nutrients support cell function and oxygen transport.

items.title: Provides potassium and magnesium
items.content: These minerals support normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Slow-digesting carbohydrates
items.content: Pigeon peas have a relatively low glycemic index, so they raise blood sugar more slowly.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Pigeon peas contain fermentable carbohydrates that may cause gas or bloating, especially if you are not used to them.

items.title: Must be cooked
items.content: Raw or undercooked legumes can cause digestive upset, so soak dried peas and cook them thoroughly.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Pigeon pea allergy is uncommon but can occur, and people allergic to other legumes may also react.

items.title: Reduced mineral absorption
items.content: Pigeon peas contain phytates that can reduce mineral absorption, which soaking and cooking help lessen.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried pigeon peas can be soaked and simmered until tender for soups, stews, and curries, and split toor dal can be cooked into dal with spices. Fresh or frozen green pigeon peas can be added to rice dishes, stews, and sautés. Season them near the end of cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried pigeon peas in an airtight container in a cool, dry place, where they keep for a year or longer. Cooked pigeon peas should be refrigerated in an airtight container and eaten within three to five days, or frozen. Keep fresh pods in the refrigerator for a few days.
